title.narrative: TLP Niger, My voice, my right

description.narrative:
The main objective of the “My Voice, My Right” project is to promote the full enjoyment of individual and collective freedoms of citizens, particularly young people, mainly through the creation of a multi-actor exchange framework for the opening up and protectionof Niger's civic space and through the organization of a sub-regional forum on civic space.
TLP intends to carry out a broad advocacy campaign at the local, regional, and international levels on the recommendations of the forum on civic space.
The project will also strengthen the capacities of decentralized legal coordinations to better equip them to defend and protect civic space.
Finally, the project will focus on raising awareness on good governance for a consistent and responsible citizen mobilization by organizingregional public debates.
It will therefore be a matter of 1. Organize a multi-stakeholder forum (CSOs and the state) on the shrinking civic space in Niger. 2. Continue the establishment of departmental and communal coordination by all regional coordination. 3. 3. Organize conferences and open debates on citizen participation in local governance. 4. Strengthen the capacities of TLP-Niger decentralized coordination on liberticidal laws to better influence the authorities. 5. organize training workshops for TLP-Niger web activists in digital communication techniques to better protect the virtual civic space. 6. Elaborate advocacy documents for the revision of repressive laws. 7. Organize an advocacy and awareness-raising day for actors (parliamentarians, political decision-makers, etc.) on freedom-destroying laws to consider their revision. 8. Create tools to popularize rights.
At the end of the project, it ishoped that citizens and civil society organisations will be able to organise, participate, communicate without hindrance, claim their rights and influence the political and social structures around them.

participating-org.narrative:
The Tournons la Page coalition in Niger is an integral part of the "Let's Turn the Page" campaign, an international citizen movement present in Africa and Europe, promoting alternation and good democratic practices. created in 2014, Tournons is currentlypresentedin 8 African countries (Burundi, Cameroon, Congo-Brazzaville, Gabon, DRC, Chad, Niger-and Ivory Coast) and in Europe. It has more than 220 member organizations and partners with many powerful and legitimate NGOs (Secours Catholique-Caritas France, Misereor, Amnesty International, Front Line Defender, ACAT, Survival, etc.). In Niger, Tournons la Page's national coalition brings together 14 human rights organizations, labor unions, women, youth, journalists and artists. The number of activists through the structures is estimated at 3000, distributed in all regions, departments and communes of Niger. TLP Niger has also developed a strategic partnership of mobilization with certain local partners such as the Confederation of Workers of Niger (CNT),the General Confederation of Workers of Niger (CGT-Niger) and the Collective of Organizations for the Defense of Human Rights. Man and Democracy (CODDHD)
The national coalition of Tournons La Page Niger is also attached to the international coordination of TLP. As a technical body hosted by Secours Catholique-Caritas France in Paris, the international coordination assists all national coalitions, including the Nigerien coalition, in carrying out its activities. It did away with the know-how and skillsof Catholic secrets to assist actors in the field on theiradvocacy activities. International coordination also plays a role in the internal sharing of information and practices of TLP members and the defense of members in the event of a physical, judicialor psychological threat.
